body.text: For Hobart musician, poet and educator Daniel Townsend, International Day of People with Disability (IDPwD) is more than a date on the calendar; it is a celebration of resilience, identity and belonging.
Daniel is one of 18 external content creators with disability recruited to produce content for the ABC as part of its partnership with the Department of Health, Disability and Ageing.
Working in paid roles across News, Audio and Screen, the creators are producing stories that bring lived experience and fresh perspectives to audiences across Australia.
"Having a disability is work all the time, and that's why we get strong. This is a day for us," Daniel said.
"I hope people see something of themselves in me, that my journey lights up something in them, and that they choose to face the scary cave and go treasure hunting too … there will be dragons."

In collaboration with ABC Radio Hobart, Daniel is developing content exploring his experience of being discouraged from pursuing music because of his disability, and the importance of seeing disability represented authentically in the industries and communities people love.
"Storytelling is always there at the start of social change," he said.
"We need to tell the kind of stories we want to live."
About IDPwD
December 3 is the United Nations International Day of People with Disability, a day dedicated to increasing awareness, understanding and acceptance of people with disability.

The UN's 2026 theme, The CRPD at 20: Building on Progress, Advancing the Future, marks 20 years since countries including Australia adopted the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (CRPD).
The agreement affirms people with disability have the same rights as everyone else and should be able to participate fully in all areas of life.
The theme reflects on the progress made over the past two decades while recognising the work still needed to achieve full inclusion and equality.
This year's ABC coverage will recognise the experiences, achievements, challenges and contributions of the 5.5 million Australians living with disability.
For more information, visit the United Nations website.
What the ABC is doing
From November 19 to December 10, disability stories will feature across ABC platforms, with content spanning television, radio, digital and social media.
Over the next three weeks, hundreds of digital articles from ABC journalists and IDPwD 2026 content creators will be published across ABC platforms.
Sport commentator and IDPwD content creator Oliver Walker-Peel teamed up with ABC Sport to produce a feature on the Special Olympics.
ABC social channels are showcasing disability-led storytelling, with Abbey Faulkner interviewing NRL and NRLW stars at the Dally M Awards.
James Houghton has produced content for Behind The News, including a feature on magpie-swooping season, several classroom stories, and a story for BTN's media literacy special.
Among the IDPwD creators is Brittany Goh, a performer, disability advocate and the first wheelchair user to graduate from the National Institute of Dramatic Art's diploma of musical theatre.
Working with Compass, Brittany is creating content exploring how accessibility can enrich learning, creativity and opportunity.
"Representation creates a path forward," she said.
"When people see disability in the media, arts, on stage, on screen and behind the scenes, they can imagine a future for themselves there too."
Disability advocate and university student Breanna Medcalfe will launch the ABC's IDPwD coverage on November 19 with content produced across ABC Sunshine Coast.

After interviewing rapper and disability advocate MC Wheels at the Strummingbird music festival, Breanna produced a TV story exploring accessibility at live music events and the difference inclusive design can make.
She is also producing more content for IDPwD and will play a key role in ABC Radio Queensland's IDPwD broadcast.

The Assembly's Jackson Hughes is collaborating with ABC Sunshine Coast's Braedan Jason on a series of interviews, including conversations with Australian para-canoeist and former soldier Curtis McGrath and disability advocate Shane Hryhorec.
One half of the viral social media duo from Two Mates 1 Chair, Fletcher Crowley, will create content and co-present a special edition of triple j hack.

Elsewhere, Maizy Randle is gaining hands-on production experience with Back Roads, and ABC International is collaborating with Papua New Guinea para-athlete of the year Dorna Longbut on a story for ABC Pacific.

Audiences can also expect disability-focused content across ABC radio networks, a refreshed Spotify playlist featuring musicians with disability, and programming including a dedicated disability collection on iview.

ABC's IDPwD content creators will produce interviews, packages and co-present for ABC Hobart, ABC Canberra, triple j hack, ABC North Queensland and ABC Sunshine Coast, with transcripts available for on-demand audio content.
The Logie Award-winning ABC iview series The Assembly is filming its fourth season.
ABC Kids has launched Bluey's Auslan Sign & Seek, a fun and interactive way for families to learn Australian Sign Language (Auslan) together.
The playful game is narrated by the voice of Jack's dad, comedian Hamish Blake.
Our Storyteller Scholarship
The IDPwD partnership also funds the ABC Storyteller Scholarship for two early-career content creators with disability.

Brendan Bernier, working with ABC North Queensland, has produced radio pieces on a huge array of topics including accessible travel and triathlons for low-vision athletes, plus the ABC's national IDPwD radio promotional ad.

Julie Dickson, working with ABC Lifestyle, has produced articles and social content on various topics including a perspective piece on dwarfism and a video on Instagram with tips to help you read more.
